title: Battleship: server-authority attack resolution
description:
When a player attacks a coordinate, the server checks the opponent hidden grid and returns hit/miss. The attacker cannot verify the result independently — this is pure Tier 3 trust.

## Attack flow
1. Attacker sends: Fire action at coordinate (e.g. B4)
2. Server looks up opponent ocean grid at B4
3. If ship segment present: HIT — mark segment as damaged, place hit marker on attacker target grid
4. If empty: MISS — place miss marker on attacker target grid
5. If all segments of a ship are damaged: announce "carrier sunk" (reveal ship type, not positions)
6. Broadcast result to both players (hit/miss at coordinate, sunk announcement if applicable)

## What the attacker sees
- Their target grid updated with hit/miss marker at the coordinate
- If sunk: which ship type was sunk
- They do NOT see the opponent ocean grid

## What the defender sees
- Their ocean grid shows damage to their ship segment
- They see the attack coordinate

## Server vault integration
Ship positions stored in the vault as hidden facts. Attack resolution reads from vault. This is exactly what the vault was designed for.

## Duplicate attack prevention
Attacking the same coordinate twice should be rejected ("already attacked B4").

## Test
Place ships for both players. Player 1 attacks B4 (hit). Verify hit marker on player 1 target grid. Verify player 1 cannot see player 2 ocean. Attack same cell again — verify rejection.
close_reason: Fire action handler implemented in both Rust and Python engines. Checks opponent ocean grid, places hit/miss peg on attacker target grid, increments hit_count on ship component, prevents duplicate fires. Tested with hit, miss, and duplicate rejection tests.
